g.text: Three tiers, no persistence layer. Domain logic is pure and framework-free, so it can be tested without a server, a network or a key.
React 18 · Next.js App Router · no build-step CSS
Flow state machine: form → code → report
Holds tokens in memory only — never storage
Password hashed here; only the first
5 hash characters ever leave the device
Interface text in six languages, plus the trust copy,
annotated with the file that backs each claim
HTTPS · HSTS · CSP · address, code, signed tokens — never a password
Stateless · fails closed · no filesystem, no database
HTTP ROUTES — thin: validate, limit, delegate
Looks up, scores, signs the report
DOMAIN LOGIC — pure functions, no framework, no I/O (except sources.js)
Routes never compute. Every figure the user sees originates in score.js or playbook.js, which is why the agent cannot invent one.
No database, no object store, no session store, no analytics, no cookies, no localStorage. State that must survive a step is signed
and handed back to the browser. The only server-side residue is rate-limit counters keyed by HMAC hash, expiring within 24 hours.
Each is optional; the system degrades rather than fails
ASSURANCE — RUNS OFFLINE, NO KEYS, NO NETWORK
Possible because the domain logic is pure
What can a bad model do?
Dependencies: next · react · react-dom. No ORM, no database driver, no ML runtime — the scoring model is a published formula, not a trained artefact.
Security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy) are set in next.config.js and verified against the deployed site.
